full_narration: Why can a yawn from across the workbench make you yawn too? The answer is a reflex with a social side. Scientists call it contagious yawning. Seeing, hearing, or thinking about a yawn can trigger one. Your brain constantly tracks other people's faces and actions. Researchers think social attention helps prime your own yawn response. The exact brain mechanism is still unsettled. It is not simply caused by low oxygen. That old explanation did not survive experiments. Chimpanzees and bonobos can catch yawns too. So a visible yawn can become a social chain reaction. Your brain may join in before you decide to. Like and subscribe to grow more questions.
